newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mostly off on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mostly off on profit taking.

text.p: CME lumber futures settled mostly lower, pulled down in most months by profit taking following sharp gains earlier in the week, traders said.
However, seasonal considerations again lifted March to a new high, traders said.
Lumber closed $10.40 per thousand board foot lower to $1.60 higher with January off most at $433.10 and only March up at $428.90 per tbf. March posted a new high earlier of $433.50 per tbf.

The increase in January open interest Thursday was considered commercial hedge selling which prompted ideas of an overbought market, traders said. The cash market was not as strong as the futures market was indicating, they said.
Cash prices may also hit resistance starting next week as mills closed for the holidays start coming back on line.
Pit sources cited rolling of long January positions into March which added to the mixed trend in nearbys.

Lumber industry newsletter, Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $408 per tbf, up $16 from last Friday. It said buyers replenished inventories that had dwindled during December. However, it added that many buyers stood aside, waiting to see how futures react to a full week of production.
